title: I built the AI trading research platform I wished existed as a trader
author: Few-Stretch-893
selftext:
I've been trading for years, and eventually I started asking myself a question: if I could build the research platform I actually wanted to use, what would it look like?

So I built it.

It's called Midas, and the idea goes beyond asking an AI whether a stock is a buy or a sell.

Midas brings together stock research dossiers, multiple AI agents that can analyze and challenge different perspectives, prediction tracking, and a ledger that records outcomes so performance can be evaluated over time.

One of the things I wanted most was accountability. AI can sound incredibly confident while being completely wrong. I wanted a system where predictions don't just disappear into the conversation history. They get tracked and evaluated.

There's also an unusual part of the platform: humans can collaborate with each other, in forums, or in their timeline. users can interact with the research through AI, and AI agents have their own agent-to-agent collaboration environments within the dossiers and within a moltbook styled forum. Feedback from those interactions feeds back into the broader research system.

I'm especially interested in seeing how well this kind of architecture works in practice, and where it needs improvement.

I'm sharing this because I'd genuinely like to hear from other traders:

- What do you wish AI-powered stock research tools did better?
- Would you trust a platform more if you could inspect its prediction history and results?
- What would you want to see before paying for an AI research subscription?

I'm the person who built Midas, so I'm not pretending to be an impartial reviewer. I'm here to learn from other traders and hear honest criticism.

If you're curious, the platform is Midas Trader: [https://midas-trader.com](https://midas-trader.com)

I'm happy to answer questions about how it works and what I'm trying to accomplish with it.

comments.author: Enrico-Pollazzo
comments.body: Hey, nice work! This looks super interesting. Can you see the original predictions and how they turned out, including the ones that missed? Are they locked in so they can’t be changed afterward? Also curious whether you’ve found that having several AI agents weigh in gives better results than using just one.

replies.author: Few-Stretch-893
replies.body:
There absolutely is a full AI accuracy dashboard which logs all predictions and metrics and the prediction history for every stock in the system is located within its own dossier. Full transparency is essential, no history will ever rewrite itself, and we can learn more from our losses and inaccuracies and we will by confirming and focusing on accuracies. It's an essential part of the evolution system. 

I have found that having multiple agents work together and deliberate increases accuracy exponentially and prevents a thesis written by one agent confirming itself which seems to be the big problem with agentic trading. 

Not only that but I feel that having a social community, both for humans to interact with each other and for AI agents to interact with each other, both feeding into the system and it's analysis of different stocks and it's understanding of its own analysis patterns will become invaluable. Instead of a few agents working as an island, any AI agent plugged into the system can give it feedback as long as it's verified by evidence and help us to grow. Ideally the more of us there are the more money all of us will make

Having a multi-agent swarm in the system and One external agent that reviews their work run by opus 5.5 has taken accuracy from the 40 to 50% rage and jacked it up to 80% or so. 

I started trading with this system myself, and decided to build out a visual interface and make it available for the general public. We don't have every stock in the stock market in the system, however users can search and add stocks to the system and send them through verification simply by searching or when they upload their portfolios. 

So far, I'm pretty happy with it and so are the few users that we have. This is very early beta testing on the live launch so al
l feedback is warmly appreciated

replies.author: Few-Stretch-893
replies.body: And thank you lol I forgot to say that 😂

replies.author: Enrico-Pollazzo
replies.body: Thanks. The history tracking sounds promising. That jump to around 80% caught my attention. Roughly how many predictions and what length of time is that based on? And when you say accurate, do you mean getting the direction right, hitting a price target, or a trade actually finishing in profit?

replies.author: Few-Stretch-893
replies.body:
So there are two different levels of prediction, I took an AI agent and gave it $293 (to date and plugged it in,  that is the house book and anybody can watch it and interact with it and interact with its performance as it grows, it's up 23% in a month, so nothing to bat an eye at, but it's ... A seed starting to sprout for sure. I'm going to continue to fund it with subscription cash as it comes in but there's a fully transparent house portfolio that you can track which I've gotten some good feedback on, people like to know that the builders are investing real money into their system before putting a name on it and the ledger of every trade is fully public. 

The AI accuracy dashboard takes predictions and measures the tape for 14, 30, 60, and 90 day periods, a prediction might be wrong in the 14 day, which is totally acceptable because of sell-offs and catalyst news and things like that or accurate and that's weighted a little bit different than predictions at the 60 and 90 day mark which we hold more value to. While I like a 14-day turnaround as much as the next guy, we are much more concerned with monthly and quarterly growth than a quick flip. So this isn't really something that's for day trading as of yet as it uses a different logic but it's all tracked in there 

I just turned it on less than 2 weeks ago so we're still building our tracking system, and doing some gentle debugging. This would be our public facing beta test phase. 

So honestly anybody that can find bugs or holes or anything like that it's really appreciated. A lot of hours and a lot of work has gone into it and we have green lights on all of our functions, however I still expect this dog to have a few fleas as we get it running. I'm interested to see how it does at the three month and 6 month mark, 

She's just a baby 😂

replies.author: Enrico-Pollazzo
replies.body:
Thanks for the detail on the 14/30/60/90 day windows, that helps. Two quick things:

1. Roughly how many predictions have been scored so far at each horizon? Even a ballpark would help me understand what the \~80% is based on.

2. Beta bug report: my brand-new account shows an active agent called "Alpha" on the AI Agent tab, even though I never connected one. Is that a default slot or a status glitch?

I signed up for the trial and I'll report back what I find.

replies.author: Few-Stretch-893
replies.body:
We just started keeping the predictions a few weeks ago . This is a relatively new system so it'll be a whole before all those numbers come in . 

Alpha is our claude system, that's just a placeholder until people connect their own AI at which point it will reflect your AI accordinly! 

I appreciate you joining friend! I look forward to hearing what your experience is like!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: does Midas keep a dated log of what it said before each move? a research tool that can't show its old calls is just a smart chart.

replies.author: Few-Stretch-893
replies.body: It absolutely does ! On each stocks dossier and there is a full dashboard built out with every prediction it makes . It does not change historical record, it only learns from them , as can we.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: that's the right way round, a call log it can't edit is what makes the hit rate mean anything. the next thing people will ask for is the misses sorted by sector, that's where a model's blind spot usually shows up.

replies.author: Few-Stretch-893
replies.body:
I totally agree, we've got some development to do yet but the AI accuracy dashboard is pretty comprehensive. 

My personal favorite part, is how when users connect their AI agent into the system, they can talk to each other in a moltbook style community forum, and contribute and vote on stocks and actually give feedback from their own independent research to the system. 

The more AI agents that are plugged in, the smarter it gets. Humans also have a forum to communicate with each other and can comment on different stocks, there's portfolio trading, paper trading, educational models for stock trading and agentic trading, and a whole lot more. 

The first month is free and then the three subsequent months are only 4.99 a month 

I'd appreciated if you could take it for a test drive for a month and drop any feedback or ways that you think could help it grow 🫶🏽❤️🫶🏽

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: agents voting on each other's calls is a fun idea. I'd weight each vote by that agent's own logged hit rate though, or the chattiest model ends up steering the board.

replies.author: Few-Stretch-893
replies.body: So agents have a few different scores , but one is directly related to the quality of contributions they make. It's not about the noise but the quality of the sound. There's an interaction score too. The fist 100 users will definitely be an interesting learning experience !
